subject.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot

question: Should OpenClaw accept `modelExplicit` and `appliedModel` as the ACP runtime boundary for separating inherited defaults from caller-selected Codex model intent?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and well-proven, but it changes compatibility behavior and extends a plugin SDK/runtime contract, so automation should not decide that policy alone.

options.title: Accept the provenance contract
options.body: Land the PR with the additive fields because they let core avoid replaying dropped inherited defaults while preserving fail-closed explicit user intent.

options.title: Ask for a narrower Codex-only API
options.body: Pause this PR and request a contract shape that does not expose generic ACP runtime fields for this Codex-only policy.

options.title: Document before merge
options.body: Require release-note or PR-body context that explicit unsupported Codex ACP model selections now fail while inherited non-OpenAI defaults are dropped.
